title.heading: PUBLIC SAFETY COMMUNICATIONS AND ELECTROMAGNETIC SPECTRUM AUCTIONS

section.heading: DEFINITIONS.

paragraph.heading: 700 mhz band.—
paragraph.content: The term “700 MHz band” means the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies from 698 megahertz to 806 megahertz.

paragraph.heading: 700 mhz d block spectrum.—
paragraph.content: The term “700 MHz D block spectrum” means the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies from 758 megahertz to 763 megahertz and between the frequencies from 788 megahertz to 793 megahertz.

paragraph.heading: Appropriate committees of congress.—
paragraph.chapeau: Except as otherwise specifically provided, the term “appropriate committees of Congress” means—

subparagraph.content: the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate; and
the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives.

paragraph.heading: Assistant secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Assistant Secretary” means the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information.

paragraph.heading: Board.—
paragraph.content: The term “Board” means the Board of the First Responder Network Authority established under section 6204(b).

paragraph.heading: Broadcast television licensee.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “broadcast television licensee” means the licensee of—

subparagraph.content: a full-power television station; or
a low-power television station that has been accorded primary status as a Class A television licensee under section 73.6001(a) of title 47, Code of Federal Regulations.

paragraph.heading: Broadcast television spectrum.—
paragraph.content: The term “broadcast television spectrum” means the portions of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies from 54 megahertz to 72 megahertz, from 76 megahertz to 88 megahertz, from 174 megahertz to 216 megahertz, and from 470 megahertz to 698 megahertz.

paragraph.heading: Commercial mobile data service.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “commercial mobile data service” means any mobile service (as defined in section 3 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 153)) that is—

subparagraph.content: a data service;
provided for profit; and
available to the public or such classes of eligible users as to be effectively available to a substantial portion of the public, as specified by regulation by the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Commercial mobile service.—
paragraph.content: The term “commercial mobile service” has the meaning given such term in section 332 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 332).

paragraph.heading: Commercial standards.—
paragraph.content: The term “commercial standards” means the technical standards followed by the commercial mobile service and commercial mobile data service industries for network, device, and Internet Protocol connectivity. Such term includes standards developed by the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the Alliance for Telecommunications Industry Solutions (ATIS), the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).

paragraph.heading: Commission.—
paragraph.content: The term “Commission” means the Federal Communications Commission.

paragraph.heading: Core network.—
paragraph.content: The term “core network” means the core network described in section 6202(b)(1).

paragraph.heading: Emergency call.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “emergency call” means any real-time communication with a public safety answering point or other emergency management or response agency, including—

subparagraph.content: through voice, text, or video and related data; and
nonhuman-initiated automatic event alerts, such as alarms, telematics, or sensor data, which may also include real-time voice, text, or video communications.

paragraph.heading: Existing public safety broadband spectrum.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “existing public safety broadband spectrum” means the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies—

subparagraph.content: from 763 megahertz to 768 megahertz;
from 793 megahertz to 798 megahertz;
from 768 megahertz to 769 megahertz; and
from 798 megahertz to 799 megahertz.

paragraph.heading: First responder network authority.—
paragraph.content: The term “First Responder Network Authority” means the First Responder Network Authority established under section 6204.

paragraph.heading: Forward auction.—
paragraph.content: The term “forward auction” means the portion of an incentive auction of broadcast television spectrum under section 6403(c).

paragraph.heading: Incentive auction.—
paragraph.content: The term “incentive auction” means a system of competitive bidding under subparagraph (G) of section 309(j)(8) of the Communications Act of 1934, as added by section 6402.

paragraph.heading: Interoperability board.—
paragraph.content: The term “Interoperability Board” means the Technical Advisory Board for First Responder Interoperability established under section 6203.

paragraph.heading: Multichannel video programming distributor.—
paragraph.content: The term “multichannel video programming distributor” has the meaning given such term in section 602 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 522).

paragraph.heading: Narrowband spectrum.—
paragraph.content: The term “narrowband spectrum” means the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies from 769 megahertz to 775 megahertz and between the frequencies from 799 megahertz to 805 megahertz.

paragraph.heading: Nationwide public safety broadband network.—
paragraph.content: The term “nationwide public safety broadband network” means the nationwide, interoperable public safety broadband network described in section 6202.

paragraph.heading: Next generation 9-1-1 services.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Next Generation 9-1-1 services” means an IP-based system comprised of hardware, software, data, and operational policies and procedures that—

subparagraph.content: provides standardized interfaces from emergency call and message services to support emergency communications;
processes all types of emergency calls, including voice, text, data, and multimedia information;
acquires and integrates additional emergency call data useful to call routing and handling;
delivers the emergency calls, messages, and data to the appropriate public safety answering point and other appropriate emergency entities;
supports data or video communications needs for coordinated incident response and management; and
provides broadband service to public safety answering points or other first responder entities.

paragraph.heading: NIST.—
paragraph.content: The term “NIST” means the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

paragraph.heading: NTIA.—
paragraph.content: The term “NTIA” means the National Telecommunications and Information Administration.

paragraph.heading: Public safety answering point.—
paragraph.content: The term “public safety answering point” has the meaning given such term in section 222 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 222).

paragraph.heading: Public safety entity.—
paragraph.content: The term “public safety entity” means an entity that provides public safety services.

paragraph.heading: Public safety services.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “public safety services”—

subparagraph.content: has the meaning given the term in section 337(f) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 337(f)); and
includes services provided by emergency response providers, as that term is defined in section 2 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 101).

paragraph.heading: Public safety trust fund.—
paragraph.content: The term “Public Safety Trust Fund” means the trust fund established under section 6413(a)(1).

paragraph.heading: Radio access network.—
paragraph.content: The term “radio access network” means the radio access network described in section 6202(b)(2).

paragraph.heading: Reverse auction.—
paragraph.content: The term “reverse auction” means the portion of an incentive auction of broadcast television spectrum under section 6403(a), in which a broadcast television licensee may submit bids stating the amount it would accept for voluntarily relinquishing some or all of its broadcast television spectrum usage rights.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” has the meaning given such term in section 3 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 153).

paragraph.heading: Ultra high frequency.—
paragraph.content: The term “ultra high frequency” means, with respect to a television channel, that the channel is located in the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies from 470 megahertz to 698 megahertz.

paragraph.heading: Very high frequency.—
paragraph.content: The term “very high frequency” means, with respect to a television channel, that the channel is located in the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the frequencies from 54 megahertz to 72 megahertz, from 76 megahertz to 88 megahertz, or from 174 megahertz to 216 megahertz.

section.heading: RULE OF CONSTRUCTION.
section.content: Each range of frequencies described in this title shall be construed to be inclusive of the upper and lower frequencies in the range.

section.heading: ENFORCEMENT.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Commission shall implement and enforce this title as if this title is a part of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 151 et seq.). A violation of this title, or a regulation promulgated under this title, shall be considered to be a violation of the Communications Act of 1934, or a regulation promulgated under such Act, respectively.

paragraph.heading: Other agencies.—
paragraph.content: Subsection (a) does not apply in the case of a provision of this title that is expressly required to be carried out by an agency (as defined in section 551 of title 5, United States Code) other than the Commission.

paragraph.heading: NTIA regulations.—
paragraph.content: The Assistant Secretary may promulgate such regulations as are necessary to implement and enforce any provision of this title that is expressly required to be carried out by the Assistant Secretary.

section.heading: NATIONAL SECURITY RESTRICTIONS ON USE OF FUNDS AND AUCTION PARTICIPATION.

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.content: No funds made available by subtitle B or C may be used to make payments under a contract to a person described in subsection (c).

subsection.heading: Auction Participation.—
subsection.chapeau: A person described in subsection (c) may not participate in a system of competitive bidding under section 309(j) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 309(j))—

paragraph.content: that is required to be conducted by this title; or
in which any spectrum usage rights for which licenses are being assigned were made available under clause (i) of subparagraph (G) of paragraph (8) of such section, as added by section 6402.

subsection.heading: Person Described.—
subsection.content: A person described in this subsection is a person who has been, for reasons of national security, barred by any agency of the Federal Government from bidding on a contract, participating in an auction, or receiving a grant.

section.heading: REALLOCATION OF D BLOCK TO PUBLIC SAFETY.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Commission shall reallocate the 700 MHz D block spectrum for use by public safety entities in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

subsection.heading: Spectrum Allocation.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 337(a) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 337(a)) is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking “24” in paragraph (1) and inserting “34”; and
by striking “36” in paragraph (2) and inserting “26”.

section.heading: FLEXIBLE USE OF NARROWBAND SPECTRUM.
section.content: The Commission may allow the narrowband spectrum to be used in a flexible manner, including usage for public safety broadband communications, subject to such technical and interference protection measures as the Commission may require.

section.heading: SINGLE PUBLIC SAFETY WIRELESS NETWORK LICENSEE.

subsection.heading: Reallocation and Grant of License.—
subsection.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, and subject to the provisions of this Act, the Commission shall reallocate and grant a license to the First Responder Network Authority for the use of the 700 MHz D block spectrum and existing public safety broadband spectrum.

paragraph.heading: Initial license.—
paragraph.content: The license granted under subsection (a) shall be for an initial term of 10 years from the date of the initial issuance of the license.

paragraph.heading: Renewal of license.—
paragraph.content: Prior to expiration of the term of the initial license granted under subsection (a) or the expiration of any subsequent renewal of such license, the First Responder Network Authority shall submit to the Commission an application for the renewal of such license. Such renewal application shall demonstrate that, during the preceding license term, the First Responder Network Authority has met the duties and obligations set forth under this Act. A renewal license granted under this paragraph shall be for a term of not to exceed 10 years.

subsection.heading: Facilitation of Transition.—
subsection.content: The Commission shall take all actions necessary to facilitate the transition of the existing public safety broadband spectrum to the First Responder Network Authority.

section.heading: PUBLIC SAFETY BROADBAND NETWORK.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall ensure the establishment of a nationwide, interoperable public safety broadband network.

subsection.heading: Network Components.—
subsection.chapeau: The nationwide public safety broadband network shall be based on a single, national network architecture that evolves with technological advancements and initially consists of—

paragraph.chapeau: a core network that—

subparagraph.content: consists of national and regional data centers, and other elements and functions that may be distributed geographically, all of which shall be based on commercial standards; and

subparagraph.chapeau: provides the connectivity between—

clause.content: the radio access network; and
the public Internet or the public switched network, or both; and

paragraph.chapeau: a radio access network that—

subparagraph.content: consists of all cell site equipment, antennas, and backhaul equipment, based on commercial standards, that are required to enable wireless communications with devices using the public safety broadband spectrum; and

shall be developed, constructed, managed, maintained, and operated taking into account the plans developed in the State, local, and tribal planning and implementation grant program under section 6302(a).

section.heading: PUBLIC SAFETY INTEROPERABILITY BOARD.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: There is established within the Commission an advisory board to be known as the “Technical Advisory Board for First Responder Interoperability”.

subparagraph.heading: Voting members.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this title, the Chairman of the Commission shall appoint 14 voting members to the Interoperability Board, of which—

clause.chapeau: 4 members shall be representatives of wireless providers, of which—

subclause.content: 2 members shall be representatives of national wireless providers;
1 member shall be a representative of regional wireless providers; and
1 member shall be a representative of rural wireless providers;

clause.content: 3 members shall be representatives of equipment manufacturers;

clause.chapeau: 4 members shall be representatives of public safety entities, of which—

subclause.content: not less than 1 member shall be a representative of management level employees of public safety entities; and
not less than 1 member shall be a representative of employees of public safety entities;

clause.content: 3 members shall be representatives of State and local governments, chosen to reflect geographic and population density differences across the United States; and

all members shall have specific expertise necessary to developing technical requirements under this section, such as technical expertise, public safety communications expertise, and commercial network experience.

subparagraph.heading: Non-voting member.—
subparagraph.content: The Assistant Secretary shall appoint 1 non-voting member to the Interoperability Board.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), members of the Interoperability Board shall be appointed for the life of the Interoperability Board.

subparagraph.heading: Removal for cause.—
subparagraph.content: A member of the Interoperability Board may be removed for cause upon the determination of the Chairman of the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Vacancies.—
paragraph.content: Any vacancy in the Interoperability Board shall not affect the powers of the Interoperability Board, and shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment.

paragraph.heading: Chairperson and vice chairperson.—
paragraph.content: The Interoperability Board shall select a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson from among the members of the Interoperability Board.

paragraph.heading: Quorum.—
paragraph.content: A majority of the members of the Interoperability Board shall constitute a quorum.

paragraph.heading: Development of technical requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Interoperability Board, in consultation with the NTIA, NIST, and the Office of Emergency Communications of the Department of Homeland Security, shall—

subparagraph.content: develop recommended minimum technical requirements to ensure a nationwide level of interoperability for the nationwide public safety broadband network; and
submit to the Commission for review in accordance with paragraph (3) recommended minimum technical requirements described in subparagraph (A).

paragraph.heading: Consideration.—
paragraph.content: In developing recommended minimum technical requirements under paragraph (1), the Interoperability Board shall base the recommended minimum technical requirements on the commercial standards for Long Term Evolution (LTE) service.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Interoperability Board submits recommended minimum technical requirements under paragraph (1)(B), the Commission shall approve the recommendations, with any revisions it deems necessary, and transmit such recommendations to the First Responder Network Authority.

subparagraph.heading: Review.—
subparagraph.content: Any actions taken under subparagraph (A) shall not be reviewable as a final agency action.

subsection.heading: Travel Expenses.—
subsection.content: The members of the Interoperability Board shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, at rates authorized for employees of agencies under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code, while away from their homes or regular places of business in the performance of services for the Interoperability Board.

subsection.heading: Exemption From Chapter 10 of Title 5, United States Code.—
subsection.content: Chapter 10 of title 5, United States Code, shall not apply to the Interoperability Board.

subsection.heading: Termination of Authority.—
subsection.content: The Interoperability Board shall terminate 15 days after the date on which the Commission transmits the recommendations to the First Responder Network Authority under subsection (c)(3)(A).

section.heading: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE FIRST RESPONDER NETWORK AUTHORITY.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: There is established as an independent authority within the NTIA the “First Responder Network Authority” or “FirstNet”.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The First Responder Network Authority shall be headed by a Board, which shall consist of—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary of Homeland Security;
the Attorney General of the United States;
the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; and
12 individuals appointed by the Secretary of Commerce in accordance with paragraph (2).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In making appointments under paragraph (1)(D), the Secretary of Commerce shall—

clause.content: appoint not fewer than 3 individuals to represent the collective interests of the States, localities, tribes, and territories;
seek to ensure geographic and regional representation of the United States in such appointments;
seek to ensure rural and urban representation in such appointments; and
appoint not fewer than 3 individuals who have served as public safety professionals.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: Each member appointed under paragraph (1)(D) should meet not less than 1 of the following criteria:

subclause.heading: Public safety experience.—
subclause.content: Knowledge and experience in the use of Federal, State, local, or tribal public safety or emergency response.

subclause.heading: Technical expertise.—
subclause.content: Technical expertise and fluency regarding broadband communications, including public safety communications.

subclause.heading: Network expertise.—
subclause.content: Expertise in building, deploying, and operating commercial telecommunications networks.

subclause.heading: Financial expertise.—
subclause.content: Expertise in financing and funding telecommunications networks.

clause.heading: Expertise to be represented.—
clause.chapeau: In making appointments under paragraph (1)(D), the Secretary of Commerce shall appoint—

subclause.content: not fewer than 1 individual who satisfies the requirement under subclause (II) of clause (i);
not fewer than 1 individual who satisfies the requirement under subclause (III) of clause (i); and
not fewer than 1 individual who satisfies the requirement under subclause (IV) of clause (i).

subparagraph.heading: Citizenship.—
subparagraph.content: No individual other than a citizen of the United States may serve as a member of the Board.

paragraph.heading: Initial appointment deadline.—
paragraph.content: Members of the Board shall be appointed not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this title.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Each member of the Board described in subparagraphs (A) through (C) of subsection (b)(1) shall serve as a member of the Board for the life of the First Responder Network Authority.

clause.heading: Appointed individuals.—
clause.content: The term of office of each individual appointed to be a member of the Board under subsection (b)(1)(D) shall be 3 years. No member described in this clause may serve more than 2 consecutive full 3-year terms.

subparagraph.heading: Expiration of term.—
subparagraph.content: Any member whose term has expired may serve until such member’s successor has taken office, or until the end of the calendar year in which such member’s term has expired, whichever is earlier.

subparagraph.heading: Appointment to fill vacancy.—
subparagraph.content: Any member appointed to fill a vacancy occurring prior to the expiration of the term for which that member’s predecessor was appointed shall be appointed for the remainder of the predecessor’s term.

subparagraph.heading: Staggered terms.—
subparagraph.chapeau: With respect to the initial members of the Board appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D)—

clause.content: 4 members shall serve for a term of 3 years;
4 members shall serve for a term of 2 years; and
4 members shall serve for a term of 1 year.

paragraph.heading: Vacancies.—
paragraph.content: A vacancy in the membership of the Board shall not affect the Board’s powers, and shall be filled in the same manner as the original member was appointed.

paragraph.heading: Selection.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of Commerce shall select, from among the members of the Board appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D), an individual to serve for a 2-year term as Chair of the Board.

paragraph.heading: Consecutive terms.—
paragraph.content: An individual may not serve for more than 2 consecutive terms as Chair of the Board.

paragraph.heading: Frequency.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Board shall meet—

subparagraph.content: at the call of the Chair; and
not less frequently than once each quarter.

paragraph.heading: Transparency.—
paragraph.content: Meetings of the Board, including any committee of the Board, shall be open to the public. The Board may, by majority vote, close any such meeting only for the time necessary to preserve the confidentiality of commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential, to discuss personnel matters, or to discuss legal matters affecting the First Responder Network Authority, including pending or potential litigation.

subsection.heading: Quorum.—
subsection.content: Eight members of the Board shall constitute a quorum, including at least 6 of the members appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The members of the Board appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D) shall be compensated at the daily rate of basic pay for level IV of the Executive Schedule for each day during which such members are engaged in performing a function of the Board.

paragraph.heading: Prohibition on compensation.—
paragraph.content: A member of the Board appointed under subparagraphs (A) through (C) of subsection (b)(1) shall serve without additional pay, and shall not otherwise benefit, directly or indirectly, as a result of their service to the First Responder Network Authority, but shall be allowed a per diem allowance for travel expenses, at rates authorized for an employee of an agency under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code, while away from the home or regular place of business of the member in the performance of the duties of the First Responder Network Authority.

section.heading: ADVISORY COMMITTEES OF THE FIRST RESPONDER NETWORK AUTHORITY.

subsection.heading: Advisory Committees.—
subsection.chapeau: The First Responder Network Authority—

paragraph.content: shall establish a standing public safety advisory committee to assist the First Responder Network Authority in carrying out its duties and responsibilities under this subtitle; and
may establish additional standing or ad hoc committees, panels, or councils as the First Responder Network Authority determines are necessary.

subsection.heading: Selection of Agents, Consultants, and Experts.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall select parties to serve as its agents, consultants, or experts in a fair, transparent, and objective manner, and such agents may include a program manager to carry out certain of the duties and responsibilities of deploying and operating the nationwide public safety broadband network described in subsections (b) and (c) of section 6206.

paragraph.heading: Binding and final.—
paragraph.content: If the selection of an agent, consultant, or expert satisfies the requirements under paragraph (1), the selection of that agent, consultant, or expert shall be final and binding.

section.heading: POWERS, DUTIES, AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE FIRST RESPONDER NETWORK AUTHORITY.

subsection.heading: General Powers.—
subsection.chapeau: The First Responder Network Authority shall have the authority to do the following:

paragraph.content: To exercise, through the actions of its Board, all powers specifically granted by the provisions of this subtitle, and such incidental powers as shall be necessary.

To hold such hearings, sit and act at such times and places, take such testimony, and receive such evidence as the First Responder Network Authority considers necessary to carry out its responsibilities and duties.
To obtain grants and funds from and make contracts with individuals, private companies, organizations, institutions, and Federal, State, regional, and local agencies.

To accept, hold, administer, and utilize gifts, donations, and bequests of property, both real and personal, for the purposes of aiding or facilitating the work of the First Responder Network Authority.
To spend funds under paragraph (3) in a manner authorized by the Board, but only for purposes that will advance or enhance public safety communications consistent with this title.
To take such other actions as the First Responder Network Authority (through the Board) may from time to time determine necessary, appropriate, or advisable to accomplish the purposes of this title.

subsection.heading: Duty and Responsibility to Deploy and Operate a Nationwide Public Safety Broadband Network.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The First Responder Network Authority shall hold the single public safety wireless license granted under section 6201 and take all actions necessary to ensure the building, deployment, and operation of the nationwide public safety broadband network, in consultation with Federal, State, tribal, and local public safety entities, the Director of NIST, the Commission, and the public safety advisory committee established in section 6205(a), including by, at a minimum—

subparagraph.content: ensuring nationwide standards for use and access of the network;

issuing open, transparent, and competitive requests for proposals to private sector entities for the purposes of building, operating, and maintaining the network that use, without materially changing, the minimum technical requirements developed under section 6203;
encouraging that such requests leverage, to the maximum extent economically desirable, existing commercial wireless infrastructure to speed deployment of the network; and
managing and overseeing the implementation and execution of contracts or agreements with non-Federal entities to build, operate, and maintain the network.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out the duties and responsibilities of this subsection, including issuing requests for proposals, the First Responder Network Authority shall—

subparagraph.content: ensure the safety, security, and resiliency of the network, including requirements for protecting and monitoring the network to protect against cyberattack;

subparagraph.chapeau: promote competition in the equipment market, including devices for public safety communications, by requiring that equipment for use on the network be—

clause.content: built to open, non-proprietary, commercially available standards;
capable of being used by any public safety entity and by multiple vendors across all public safety broadband networks operating in the 700 MHz band; and
backward-compatible with existing commercial networks to the extent that such capabilities are necessary and technically and economically reasonable;

subparagraph.content: promote integration of the network with public safety answering points or their equivalent; and
address special considerations for areas or regions with unique homeland security or national security needs.

paragraph.heading: Rural coverage.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out the duties and responsibilities of this subsection, including issuing requests for proposals, the nationwide, interoperable public safety broadband network, consistent with the license granted under section 6201, shall require deployment phases with substantial rural coverage milestones as part of each phase of the construction and deployment of the network. To the maximum extent economically desirable, such proposals shall include partnerships with existing commercial mobile providers to utilize cost-effective opportunities to speed deployment in rural areas.

paragraph.heading: Execution of authority.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out the duties and responsibilities of this subsection, the First Responder Network Authority may—

subparagraph.content: obtain grants from and make contracts with individuals, private companies, and Federal, State, regional, and local agencies;
hire or accept voluntary services of consultants, experts, advisory boards, and panels to aid the First Responder Network Authority in carrying out such duties and responsibilities;

subparagraph.chapeau: receive payment for use of—

clause.content: network capacity licensed to the First Responder Network Authority; and
network infrastructure constructed, owned, or operated by the First Responder Network Authority; and

subparagraph.content: take such other actions as may be necessary to accomplish the purposes set forth in this subsection.

paragraph.heading: Establishment of network policies.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out the requirements under subsection (b), the First Responder Network Authority shall develop—

subparagraph.chapeau: requests for proposals with appropriate—

clause.content: timetables for construction, including by taking into consideration the time needed to build out to rural areas and the advantages offered through partnerships with existing commercial providers under paragraph (3);
coverage areas, including coverage in rural and nonurban areas;
service levels;
performance criteria; and
other similar matters for the construction and deployment of such network;

subparagraph.content: the technical and operational requirements of the network;
practices, procedures, and standards for the management and operation of such network;
terms of service for the use of such network, including billing practices; and

subparagraph.chapeau: ongoing compliance review and monitoring of the—

clause.content: management and operation of such network;
practices and procedures of the entities operating on and the personnel using such network; and
necessary training needs of network operators and users.

subparagraph.heading: Required consultation.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In developing requests for proposals and otherwise carrying out its responsibilities under this Act, the First Responder Network Authority shall consult with regional, State, tribal, and local jurisdictions regarding the distribution and expenditure of any amounts required to carry out the policies established under paragraph (1), including with regard to the—

clause.content: construction of a core network and any radio access network build out;
placement of towers;
coverage areas of the network, whether at the regional, State, tribal, or local level;
adequacy of hardening, security, reliability, and resiliency requirements;
assignment of priority to local users;
assignment of priority and selection of entities seeking access to or use of the nationwide public safety interoperable broadband network established under subsection (b); and
training needs of local users.

subparagraph.heading: Method of consultation.—
subparagraph.content: The consultation required under subparagraph (A) shall occur between the First Responder Network Authority and the single officer or governmental body designated under section 6302(d).

paragraph.heading: Leveraging existing infrastructure.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out the requirement under subsection (b), the First Responder Network Authority shall enter into agreements to utilize, to the maximum extent economically desirable, existing—

subparagraph.content: commercial or other communications infrastructure; and
Federal, State, tribal, or local infrastructure.

paragraph.heading: Maintenance and upgrades.—
paragraph.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall ensure the maintenance, operation, and improvement of the nationwide public safety broadband network, including by ensuring that the First Responder Network Authority updates and revises any policies established under paragraph (1) to take into account new and evolving technologies.

paragraph.heading: Roaming agreements.—
paragraph.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall negotiate and enter into, as it determines appropriate, roaming agreements with commercial network providers to allow the nationwide public safety broadband network to roam onto commercial networks and gain prioritization of public safety communications over such networks in times of an emergency.

paragraph.heading: Network infrastructure and device criteria.—
paragraph.content: The Director of NIST, in consultation with the First Responder Network Authority and the Commission, shall ensure the development of a list of certified devices and components meeting appropriate protocols and standards for public safety entities and commercial vendors to adhere to, if such entities or vendors seek to have access to, use of, or compatibility with the nationwide public safety broadband network.

paragraph.heading: Representation before standard setting entities.—
paragraph.content: The First Responder Network Authority, in consultation with the Director of NIST, the Commission, and the public safety advisory committee established under section 6205(a), shall represent the interests of public safety users of the nationwide public safety broadband network before any proceeding, negotiation, or other matter in which a standards organization, standards body, standards development organization, or any other recognized standards-setting entity addresses the development of standards relating to interoperability.

paragraph.heading: Prohibition on negotiation with foreign governments.—
paragraph.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall not have the authority to negotiate or enter into any agreements with a foreign government on behalf of the United States.

subsection.heading: Exemption From Certain Laws.—
subsection.chapeau: Any action taken or decisions made by the First Responder Network Authority shall be exempt from the requirements of—

paragraph.content: section 3506 of title 44, United States Code (commonly referred to as the Paperwork Reduction Act);
chapter 5 of title 5, United States Code (commonly referred to as the Administrative Procedures Act); and
chapter 6 of title 5, United States Code (commonly referred to as the Regulatory Flexibility Act).

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund to be known as the “Network Construction Fund”.

paragraph.heading: Use of fund.—
paragraph.chapeau: Amounts deposited into the Network Construction Fund shall be used by the—

subparagraph.content: First Responder Network Authority to carry out this section, except for administrative expenses; and
NTIA to make grants to States under section 6302(e)(3)(C)(iii)(I).

subsection.heading: Termination of Authority.—
subsection.content: The authority of the First Responder Network Authority shall terminate on the date that is 15 years after the date of enactment of this title.

subsection.heading: GAO Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than 10 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report on what action Congress should take regarding the 15-year sunset of authority under subsection (f).

section.heading: INITIAL FUNDING FOR THE FIRST RESPONDER NETWORK AUTHORITY.

subsection.heading: Borrowing Authority.—
subsection.content: Prior to the deposit of proceeds into the Public Safety Trust Fund from the incentive auctions to be carried out under section 309(j)(8)(G) of the Communications Act of 1934 or the auction of spectrum pursuant to section 6401, the NTIA may borrow from the Treasury such sums as may be necessary, but not to exceed $2,000,000,000, to implement this subtitle. The NTIA shall reimburse the Treasury, without interest, from funds deposited into the Public Safety Trust Fund.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Administrative expenses of the First Responder Network Authority may not exceed $100,000,000 during the 10-year period beginning on the date of enactment of this title.

paragraph.heading: Definition.—
paragraph.content: For purposes of this subsection, the term “administrative expenses” does not include the costs incurred by the First Responder Network Authority for oversight and audits to protect against waste, fraud, and abuse.

section.heading: PERMANENT SELF-FUNDING; DUTY TO ASSESS AND COLLECT FEES FOR NETWORK USE.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Notwithstanding section 337 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 337), the First Responder Network Authority is authorized to assess and collect the following fees:

paragraph.heading: Network user fee.—
paragraph.content: A user or subscription fee from each entity, including any public safety entity or secondary user, that seeks access to or use of the nationwide public safety broadband network.

paragraph.heading: Lease fees related to network capacity.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: A fee from any entity that seeks to enter into a covered leasing agreement.

subparagraph.heading: Covered leasing agreement.—
subparagraph.chapeau: For purposes of subparagraph (A), a “covered leasing agreement” means a written agreement resulting from a public-private arrangement to construct, manage, and operate the nationwide public safety broadband network between the First Responder Network Authority and secondary user to permit—

clause.content: access to network capacity on a secondary basis for non-public safety services; and
the spectrum allocated to such entity to be used for commercial transmissions along the dark fiber of the long-haul network of such entity.

paragraph.heading: Lease fees related to network equipment and infrastructure.—
paragraph.content: A fee from any entity that seeks access to or use of any equipment or infrastructure, including antennas or towers, constructed or otherwise owned by the First Responder Network Authority resulting from a public-private arrangement to construct, manage, and operate the nationwide public safety broadband network.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Fee Amounts; Permanent Self-funding.—
subsection.content: The total amount of the fees assessed for each fiscal year pursuant to this section shall be sufficient, and shall not exceed the amount necessary, to recoup the total expenses of the First Responder Network Authority in carrying out its duties and responsibilities described under this subtitle for the fiscal year involved.

subsection.heading: Annual Approval.—
subsection.content: The NTIA shall review the fees assessed under this section on an annual basis, and such fees may only be assessed if approved by the NTIA.

subsection.heading: Required Reinvestment of Funds.—
subsection.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall reinvest amounts received from the assessment of fees under this section in the nationwide public safety interoperable broadband network by using such funds only for constructing, maintaining, operating, or improving the network.

section.heading: AUDIT AND REPORT.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary of Commerce shall enter into a contract with an independent auditor to conduct an audit, on an annual basis, of the First Responder Network Authority in accordance with general accounting principles and procedures applicable to commercial corporate transactions. Each audit conducted under this paragraph shall be made available to the appropriate committees of Congress.

paragraph.heading: Location.—
paragraph.content: Any audit conducted under paragraph (1) shall be conducted at the place or places where accounts of the First Responder Network Authority are normally kept.

paragraph.heading: Access to first responder network authority books and documents.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: For purposes of an audit conducted under paragraph (1), the representatives of the independent auditor shall—

clause.content: have access to all books, accounts, records, reports, files, and all other papers, things, or property belonging to or in use by the First Responder Network Authority that pertain to the financial transactions of the First Responder Network Authority and are necessary to facilitate the audit; and
be afforded full facilities for verifying transactions with the balances or securities held by depositories, fiscal agents, and custodians.

subparagraph.heading: Requirement.—
subparagraph.content: All books, accounts, records, reports, files, papers, and property of the First Responder Network Authority shall remain in the possession and custody of the First Responder Network Authority.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The independent auditor selected to conduct an audit under this section shall submit a report of each audit conducted under subsection (a) to—

subparagraph.content: the appropriate committees of Congress;
the President; and
the First Responder Network Authority.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each report submitted under paragraph (1) shall contain—

subparagraph.content: such comments and information as the independent auditor determines necessary to inform Congress of the financial operations and condition of the First Responder Network Authority;
any recommendations of the independent auditor relating to the financial operations and condition of the First Responder Network Authority; and

a description of any program, expenditure, or other financial transaction or undertaking of the First Responder Network Authority that was observed during the course of the audit, which, in the opinion of the independent auditor, has been carried on or made without the authority of law.

section.heading: ANNUAL REPORT TO CONGRESS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, and each year thereafter, the First Responder Network Authority shall submit an annual report covering the preceding fiscal year to the appropriate committees of Congress.

subsection.heading: Required Content.—
subsection.chapeau: The report required under subsection (a) shall include—

paragraph.content: a comprehensive and detailed report of the operations, activities, financial condition, and accomplishments of the First Responder Network Authority under this section; and
such recommendations or proposals for legislative or administrative action as the First Responder Network Authority deems appropriate.

subsection.heading: Availability to Testify.—
subsection.chapeau: The members of the Board and employees of the First Responder Network Authority shall be available to testify before the appropriate committees of the Congress with respect to—

paragraph.content: the report required under subsection (a);
the report of any audit conducted under section 6210; or
any other matter which such committees may determine appropriate.

section.heading: PUBLIC SAFETY ROAMING AND PRIORITY ACCESS.
section.chapeau: The Commission may adopt rules, if necessary in the public interest, to improve the ability of public safety networks to roam onto commercial networks and to gain priority access to commercial networks in an emergency if—

paragraph.content: the public safety entity equipment is technically compatible with the commercial network;
the commercial network is reasonably compensated; and
such access does not preempt or otherwise terminate or degrade all existing voice conversations or data sessions.

section.heading: PROHIBITION ON DIRECT OFFERING OF COMMERCIAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICE DIRECTLY TO CONSUMERS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The First Responder Network Authority shall not offer, provide, or market commercial telecommunications or information services directly to consumers.

subsection.heading: Rule of Construction.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit the First Responder Network Authority and a secondary user from entering into a covered leasing agreement pursuant to section 6208(a)(2)(B). Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the First Responder Network Authority from collecting lease fees related to network equipment and infrastructure pursuant to section 6208(a)(3).

section.heading: PROVISION OF TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE.
section.content: The Commission may provide technical assistance to the First Responder Network Authority and may take any action necessary to assist the First Responder Network Authority in effectuating its duties and responsibilities under this subtitle.

section.heading: STATE AND LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION FUND.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund to be known as the State and Local Implementation Fund.

subsection.heading: Amounts Available for State and Local Implementation Grant Program.—
subsection.content: Any amounts borrowed under subsection (c)(1) and any amounts in the State and Local Implementation Fund that are not necessary to reimburse the general fund of the Treasury for such borrowed amounts shall be available to the Assistant Secretary to implement section 6302.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Prior to the end of fiscal year 2022, the Assistant Secretary may borrow from the general fund of the Treasury such sums as may be necessary, but not to exceed $135,000,000, to implement section 6302.

paragraph.heading: Reimbursement.—
paragraph.content: The Assistant Secretary shall reimburse the general fund of the Treasury, without interest, for any amounts borrowed under paragraph (1) as funds are deposited into the State and Local Implementation Fund.

subsection.heading: Transfer of Unused Funds.—
subsection.content: If there is a balance remaining in the State and Local Implementation Fund on September 30, 2022, the Secretary of the Treasury shall transfer such balance to the general fund of the Treasury, where such balance shall be dedicated for the sole purpose of deficit reduction.

section.heading: STATE AND LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION.

subsection.heading: Establishment of State and Local Implementation Grant Program.—
subsection.content: The Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the First Responder Network Authority, shall take such action as is necessary to establish a grant program to make grants to States to assist State, regional, tribal, and local jurisdictions to identify, plan, and implement the most efficient and effective way for such jurisdictions to utilize and integrate the infrastructure, equipment, and other architecture associated with the nationwide public safety broadband network to satisfy the wireless communications and data services needs of that jurisdiction, including with regards to coverage, siting, and other needs.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Federal share of the cost of any activity carried out using a grant under this section may not exceed 80 percent of the eligible costs of carrying out that activity, as determined by the Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the First Responder Network Authority.

paragraph.heading: Waiver.—
paragraph.content: The Assistant Secretary may waive, in whole or in part, the requirements of paragraph (1) for good cause shown if the Assistant Secretary determines that such a waiver is in the public interest.

subsection.heading: Programmatic Requirements.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 6 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the First Responder Network Authority, shall establish requirements relating to the grant program to be carried out under this section, including the following:

paragraph.content: Defining eligible costs for purposes of subsection (b)(1).
Determining the scope of eligible activities for grant funding under this section.
Prioritizing grants for activities that ensure coverage in rural as well as urban areas.

subsection.heading: Certification and Designation of Officer or Governmental Body.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the grant program established under this section, the Assistant Secretary shall require each State to certify in its application for grant funds that the State has designated a single officer or governmental body to serve as the coordinator of implementation of the grant funds.

paragraph.heading: Notice.—
paragraph.chapeau: Upon the completion of the request for proposal process conducted by the First Responder Network Authority for the construction, operation, maintenance, and improvement of the nationwide public safety broadband network, the First Responder Network Authority shall provide to the Governor of each State, or his designee—

subparagraph.content: notice of the completion of the request for proposal process;
details of the proposed plan for buildout of the nationwide, interoperable broadband network in such State; and
the funding level for the State as determined by the NTIA.

paragraph.heading: State decision.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date on which the Governor of a State receives notice under paragraph (1), the Governor shall choose whether to—

subparagraph.content: participate in the deployment of the nationwide, interoperable broadband network as proposed by the First Responder Network Authority; or
conduct its own deployment of a radio access network in such State.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Upon making a decision to opt-out under paragraph (2)(B), the Governor shall notify the First Responder Network Authority, the NTIA, and the Commission of such decision.

subparagraph.heading: State request for proposals.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date on which a Governor provides notice under subparagraph (A), the Governor shall develop and complete requests for proposals for the construction, maintenance, and operation of the radio access network within the State.

subparagraph.heading: Submission and approval of alternative plan.—

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: The State shall submit an alternative plan for the construction, maintenance, operation, and improvements of the radio access network within the State to the Commission, and such plan shall demonstrate—

subclause.content: that the State will be in compliance with the minimum technical interoperability requirements developed under section 6203; and
interoperability with the nationwide public safety broadband network.

clause.heading: Commission approval or disapproval.—
clause.content: Upon submission of a State plan under clause (i), the Commission shall either approve or disapprove the plan.

clause.heading: Approval.—
clause.chapeau: If the Commission approves a plan under this subparagraph, the State—

subclause.content: may apply to the NTIA for a grant to construct the radio access network within the State that includes the showing described in subparagraph (D); and
shall apply to the NTIA to lease spectrum capacity from the First Responder Network Authority.

clause.heading: Disapproval.—
clause.content: If the Commission disapproves a plan under this subparagraph, the construction, maintenance, operation, and improvements of the network within the State shall proceed in accordance with the plan proposed by the First Responder Network Authority.

subparagraph.heading: Funding requirements.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In order to obtain grant funds and spectrum capacity leasing rights under subparagraph (C)(iii), a State shall demonstrate—

subclause.content: the technical capabilities to operate, and the funding to support, the State radio access network;
has the ability to maintain ongoing interoperability with the nationwide public safety broadband network; and
the ability to complete the project within specified comparable timelines specific to the State;

clause.content: the cost-effectiveness of the State plan submitted under subparagraph (C)(i); and
comparable security, coverage, and quality of service to that of the nationwide public safety broadband network.

subsection.heading: User Fees.—
subsection.content: If a State chooses to build its own radio access network, the State shall pay any user fees associated with State use of elements of the core network.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: A State that chooses to build its own radio access network shall not provide commercial service to consumers or offer wholesale leasing capacity of the network within the State except directly through public-private partnerships for construction, maintenance, operation, and improvement of the network within the State.

paragraph.heading: Rule of construction.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subsection shall be construed to prohibit the State and a secondary user from entering into a covered leasing agreement. Any revenue gained by the State from such a leasing agreement shall be used only for constructing, maintaining, operating, or improving the radio access network of the State.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The United States District Court for the District of Columbia shall have exclusive jurisdiction to review a decision of the Commission made under subsection (e)(3)(C)(iv).

paragraph.heading: Standard of review.—
paragraph.chapeau: The court shall affirm the decision of the Commission unless—

subparagraph.content: the decision was procured by corruption, fraud, or undue means;
there was actual partiality or corruption in the Commission; or
the Commission was guilty of misconduct in refusing to hear evidence pertinent and material to the decision or of any other misbehavior by which the rights of any party have been prejudiced.

section.heading: PUBLIC SAFETY WIRELESS COMMUNICATIONS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.

subsection.heading: NIST Directed Research and Development Program.—
subsection.content: From amounts made available from the Public Safety Trust Fund, the Director of NIST, in consultation with the Commission, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the National Institute of Justice of the Department of Justice, as appropriate, shall conduct research and assist with the development of standards, technologies, and applications to advance wireless public safety communications.

subsection.heading: Required Activities.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out the requirement under subsection (a), the Director of NIST, in consultation with the First Responder Network Authority and the public safety advisory committee established under section 6205(a), shall—

paragraph.content: document public safety wireless communications technical requirements;
accelerate the development of the capability for communications between currently deployed public safety narrowband systems and the nationwide public safety broadband network;

establish a research plan, and direct research, that addresses the wireless communications needs of public safety entities beyond what can be provided by the current generation of broadband technology;

accelerate the development of mission critical voice, including device-to-device “talkaround” capability over broadband networks, public safety prioritization, authentication capabilities, and standard application programing interfaces for the nationwide public safety broadband network, if necessary and practical;

accelerate the development of communications technology and equipment that can facilitate the eventual migration of public safety narrowband communications to the nationwide public safety broadband network; and
convene working groups of relevant government and commercial parties to achieve the requirements in paragraphs (1) through (5).

section.heading: DEADLINES FOR AUCTION OF CERTAIN SPECTRUM.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The President shall—

subparagraph.content: not later than 3 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, begin the process of withdrawing or modifying the assignment to a Federal Government station of the electromagnetic spectrum described in paragraph (2); and
not later than 30 days after completing the withdrawal or modification, notify the Commission that the withdrawal or modification is complete.

paragraph.heading: Spectrum described.—
paragraph.content: The electromagnetic spectrum described in this paragraph is the 15 megahertz of spectrum between 1675 megahertz and 1710 megahertz identified under paragraph (3).

paragraph.heading: Identification by secretary of commerce.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Commerce shall submit to the President a report identifying 15 megahertz of spectrum between 1675 megahertz and 1710 megahertz for reallocation from Federal use to non-Federal use.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Notwithstanding paragraph (15)(A) of section 309(j) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 309(j)), not later than 3 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commission shall, except as provided in paragraph (4)—

subparagraph.content: allocate the spectrum described in paragraph (2) for commercial use; and
through a system of competitive bidding under such section, grant new initial licenses for the use of such spectrum, subject to flexible-use service rules.

paragraph.heading: Spectrum described.—
paragraph.chapeau: The spectrum described in this paragraph is the following:

subparagraph.content: The frequencies between 1915 megahertz and 1920 megahertz.
The frequencies between 1995 megahertz and 2000 megahertz.
The frequencies described in subsection (a)(2).
The frequencies between 2155 megahertz and 2180 megahertz.
Fifteen megahertz of contiguous spectrum to be identified by the Commission.

paragraph.heading: Proceeds to cover 110 percent of federal relocation or sharing costs.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in paragraph (1) shall be construed to relieve the Commission from the requirements of section 309(j)(16)(B) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 309(j)(16)(B)).

paragraph.heading: Determination by commission.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Commission determines that the band of frequencies described in paragraph (2)(A) or the band of frequencies described in paragraph (2)(B) cannot be used without causing harmful interference to commercial mobile service licensees in the frequencies between 1930 megahertz and 1995 megahertz, the Commission may not—

subparagraph.content: allocate such band for commercial use under paragraph (1)(A); or
grant licenses under paragraph (1)(B) for the use of such band.

subsection.chapeau: Section 309(j)(8) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 309(j)(8)) is amended—

paragraph.content: in subparagraph (A), by striking “(D), and (E),” and inserting “(D), (E), (F), and (G),”;
in subparagraph (C)(i), by striking “subparagraph (E)(ii)” and inserting “subparagraphs (D)(ii), (E)(ii), (F), and (G)”;

paragraph.chapeau: in subparagraph (D)—

subparagraph.content: by striking the heading and inserting “Proceeds from reallocated federal spectrum.—”;

by striking “Cash” and inserting the following:
“(i) In general. Except as provided in clause (ii), cash” ; and

by adding at the end the following:
“(ii) Certain other proceeds. Notwithstanding subparagraph (A) and except as provided in subparagraph (B), in the case of proceeds (including deposits and upfront payments from successful bidders) attributable to the auction of eligible frequencies described in paragraph (2) of section 113(g) of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act that are required to be auctioned by section 6401(b)(1)(B) of the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012, such portion of such proceeds as is necessary to cover the relocation or sharing costs (as defined in paragraph (3) of such section 113(g)) of Federal entities relocated from such eligible frequencies shall be deposited in the Spectrum Relocation Fund. The remainder of such proceeds shall be deposited in the Public Safety Trust Fund established by section 6413(a)(1) of the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012.” ; and

by adding at the end the following:
